newsitem.title: USA: Florida lawmaker seeks phaseout of investments tax.
newsitem.headline: Florida lawmaker seeks phaseout of investments tax.

text.p: The chairman of Florida's Senate finance and tax subcommittee committee has proposed eliminating the state's intangibles tax on stocks, bonds and other investments.
Sen. John Ostalkiewicz, R-Orlando, said the tax discourages investment and puts Florida at a disadvantage because few other states levy it.
The first $20,000 of investments are exempt. After that, the tax is $1 per $1,000 of market value for portfolios up to $100,000 and $2 per $1,000 of assets above that amount.
The tax accounts for four percent of state revenues and is expected to bring in $981 million in fiscal 1997.

Ostalkiewicz would phase out the tax over five years by raising the exemption. The Senate's tax and finance subcommittee was scheduled to meet Thursday to discuss the proposal and other tax changes that would stimulate Florida's economy.

The proposal has already drawn fire from Republican lawmakers, especially because the tax targets wealthy individuals and corporations. Ostalkeiwicz, one of the wealthiest members of the legislature, made a fortune in the diamond business and has a net worth of $5.3 million.

In a letter to Senate President Toni Jennings, Senate Minority Leader Ken Jenne, D-Fort Lauderdale, said that although both parties are willing to cut the budget to stay within revenues, "I do not sense a willingness to reduce the budget by almost a billion dollars for the purpose of giving the most privileged people a tax break."
One-third of the revenues raised by the tax are divided among municipalities, which would be forced to raise property taxes to offset the loss of revenues, Jenne said.
Jennings, who favors eliminating the tax, said it was unlikely the measure would survive unless it included an alternate revenue source.
